title: Apple’s new smart home hardware has been finished for months. Siri was the hold-up.
excerpt: Apple is preparing a push into the smart home with a new Apple TV 4K, an updated HomePod mini, and a hub device built around its rebuilt Siri, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on Tuesday. The hardware for the first two has reportedly been finished for months and is already being tested by Apple employees on […]
content_html:
Apple is preparing a push into the smart home with a new Apple TV 4K, an updated HomePod mini, and a hub device built around its rebuilt Siri, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on Tuesday. The hardware for the first two has reportedly been finished for months and is already being tested by Apple employees on the Cupertino campus.

That detail is the story. Apple did not have a hardware problem, it had a software one, and the entire lineup sat waiting on an assistant that kept slipping.

What is coming

The new Apple TV 4K keeps the current form factor but replaces the ageing A15 with an A17 Pro or better, enough to run Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. The current box supports no Apple Intelligence features at all, so the chip upgrade is what makes the rest of the strategy possible.

It is also expected to gain more RAM and Apple’s N1 networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. The HomePod mini is a more conservative refresh, with a faster chip, an upgraded ultra-wideband chip, new colours, and no new form factor.

The hub is the ambitious part

The long-delayed smart home hub is reportedly an iPad-like device with a seven-inch square display, offered with either a wall mount or a speaker base whose hemispherical dome recalls the iMac G4. Rumoured pricing sits around $350.

It would carry a camera for video calls, facial recognition, and presence detection, and run Safari, Calendar, Photos, and Home alongside Siri AI. Apple is also reportedly designing its own security camera, potentially this year, as iOS 27 brings 4K recording, AI summaries, and cross-camera event stitching to HomeKit Secure Video.

Why it took this long

Apple finally shipped its AI do-over at WWDC in June, unveiling Siri AI as a standalone app with personal context, multi-step commands across apps, and a three-tier privacy architecture. Public release is projected for September, which is what unlocks the hardware.

The rebuilt assistant is not entirely Apple’s own. Siri now runs on a custom Gemini model of roughly 1.2 trillion parameters, licensed from Google in a deal reported at around $1 billion a year, with simple tasks staying on-device.

Some of the promised capability is still missing. Apple built a third-party AI extensions system for Siri and then declined to show it at WWDC, leaving open how much of the assistant’s app integration will exist at launch.

The European problem

There is a complication for anyone buying this hardware in the EU. Siri AI will not be available on iPhone or iPad in the European Union when iOS 27 ships, and this time Apple has given no timeline.

That leaves European customers facing a smart home lineup whose central selling point is an assistant they cannot yet use. A faster Apple TV is still a faster Apple TV, but the case for the hub in particular rests almost entirely on Siri AI.

The competitive position

Apple is arriving late to a market that reorganised without it. Amazon and Google spent years expanding Alexa and Google Assistant into broader AI ecosystems while HomePod and Siri largely stood still.

The interoperability question has also moved on. Matter-certified devices now work across Apple, Google, Amazon, and Samsung ecosystems without extra configuration, shifting competition from device compatibility towards software quality and assistant capability.

That shift should favour whoever has the best assistant. It is not obvious that Apple can claim that, having licensed its frontier model from a direct competitor in the smart home market.

When it might land

The Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini could arrive as soon as September, potentially alongside the iPhone launch. Apple often holds a second autumn event, usually for iPads or Macs, and a home-focused October event is a plausible alternative given how many devices are queued.

None of this is confirmed. Apple has not announced any of these products, timelines have slipped repeatedly before, and the reporting rests on people familiar with plans that Apple itself has changed more than once.

content_html_zh:
据彭博社的 Mark Gurman 周二报道，苹果正准备推出新的 Apple TV 4K、更新的 HomePod mini 以及围绕重建的 Siri 构建的集线器设备，进军智能家居领域。 据报道，前两个的硬件已经完成了几个月，并且已经由库比蒂诺园区的苹果员工进行了测试。

这个细节就是故事。 苹果没有硬件问题，而是软件问题，整个阵容都在等待一个不断下滑的助手。

即将发生什么

新款 Apple TV 4K 保留了当前的外形尺寸，但用 A17 Pro 或更好的处理器取代了老化的 A15，足以运行 Apple Intelligence 和 Siri AI。 当前的盒子根本不支持Apple Intelligence功能，因此芯片升级使该策略的其余部分成为可能。

它还有望获得更多 RAM 和苹果 N1 网络芯片，带来 Wi-Fi 7、蓝牙 6 和 Thread。 HomePod mini 是一种更为保守的更新，具有更快的芯片、升级的超宽带芯片、新的颜色，但没有新的外形。

枢纽是雄心勃勃的部分

据报道，这款拖延已久的智能家居中心是一款类似 iPad 的设备，配有 7 英寸方形显示屏，配有壁挂式支架或扬声器底座，其半球形圆顶让人想起 iMac G4。 传闻定价约为 350 美元。

它将配备用于视频通话、面部识别和存在检测的摄像头，并与 Siri AI 一起运行 Safari、日历、照片和 Home。 据报道，苹果还可能在今年设计自己的安全摄像头，因为 iOS 27 为 HomeKit 安全视频带来了 4K 录制、人工智能摘要和跨摄像头事件拼接功能。

为什么花了这么长时间

苹果最终在 6 月份的 WWDC 上推出了 AI 改造，推出了 Siri AI 作为一款独立应用程序，具有个人上下文、跨应用程序的多步骤命令以及三层隐私架构。 预计将于 9 月公开发布，届时将解锁硬件。

重建后的助手并不完全是苹果自己的。 Siri 现在运行在一个包含约 1.2 万亿个参数的定制 Gemini 模型上，该模型由谷歌以每年约 10 亿美元的价格获得许可，简单的任务保留在设备上。

一些承诺的功能仍然缺失。 苹果为 Siri 构建了第三方人工智能扩展系统，但拒绝在 WWDC 上展示该系统，因此在发布时该助手的应用程序集成程度仍不确定。

欧洲问题

对于任何在欧盟购买这种硬件的人来说，都会遇到一些麻烦。 当 iOS 27 发布时，Siri AI 将无法在欧盟的 iPhone 或 iPad 上使用，这次苹果没有给出时间表。

这使得欧洲客户面临着一个智能家居系列，其核心卖点是他们还无法使用的助手。 更快的 Apple TV 仍然是更快的 Apple TV，但该中心的情况几乎完全取决于 Siri AI。

竞争地位

苹果公司在没有它的情况下重组的市场来得太晚了。 亚马逊和谷歌花了数年时间将 Alexa 和 Google Assistant 扩展到更广泛的人工智能生态系统，而 HomePod 和 Siri 基本上停滞不前。

互操作性问题也随之而来。 Matter 认证的设备现在可以在苹果、谷歌、亚马逊和三星生态系统中运行，无需额外配置，将竞争从设备兼容性转向软件质量和助手功能。

这种转变应该有利于拥有最好助手的人。 苹果公司从智能家居市场的直接竞争对手那里获得了其前沿模型的许可，因此尚不清楚它是否可以声称这一点。

什么时候可能落地

Apple TV 4K 和 HomePod mini 最快将于 9 月上市，可能与 iPhone 一起发布。 苹果经常举办第二次秋季活动，通常针对 iPad 或 Mac，考虑到排队的设备数量，以家庭为中心的 10 月活动是一个合理的选择。

这些都没有得到证实。 苹果尚未宣布任何此类产品，之前的时间表也曾多次推迟，而知情人士透露，苹果本身已经不止一次改变了计划。
